overview: A brushless motor replaces the mechanical brushes of a regular DC motor with electronic commutation — a controller rapidly switches power across three coil phases in the right sequence to spin the rotor. That removes the wear-prone part that limits a brushed motor's lifespan and lets BLDCs run more efficiently at much higher speeds, which is exactly why every drone propeller and most high-performance robots use them. The tradeoff is that a BLDC motor cannot be driven directly from a microcontroller pin or even a simple H-bridge — it requires a dedicated Electronic Speed Controller (ESC) that handles the three-phase commutation, typically itself controlled by a simple PWM or digital signal.
simpleSummary: A powerful, efficient motor with no wearing brushes inside, spun by rapidly switching power through its coils.

specifications.phases: 3 (three coil windings, star or delta wound)
specifications.kvRating: Motor constant in RPM per volt (e.g. 1000KV = ~1000 RPM per volt, unloaded)
specifications.operatingVoltage: Model-dependent, commonly driven from 2S-6S LiPo packs (7.4V-22.2V)
specifications.controlRequirement: Requires an ESC (Electronic Speed Controller) — cannot be driven directly
specifications.efficiency: Higher than brushed DC motors, less heat, longer lifespan (no brush wear)

pinMap.name: Phase A
pinMap.function: One of three motor phase windings, connects to the ESC.
pinMap.currentLimit: Motor's rated current (varies widely by size)
pinMap.gotcha: The three phase wires are often unlabeled/interchangeable on many hobby motors — swapping any two reverses the spin direction.

useCases.title: Drone/multirotor propulsion
useCases.scenario: The standard motor type for every quadcopter/drone propeller, chosen for its power-to-weight ratio.

useCases.title: High-performance robot wheel drive
useCases.scenario: Combined with a gearbox or direct-drive hub design for robots needing more speed/efficiency than a brushed motor provides.

useCases.title: Gimbal stabilization
useCases.scenario: Specialized low-KV gimbal BLDC motors provide smooth, precise camera stabilization.

oftenConfusedWith: DC geared motor (brushed, 2-wire, no ESC needed)
Stepper motors (open-loop positioning, not continuous high-speed spin)
oftenUpgradedTo: FOC (Field-Oriented Control) ESCs for smoother, more efficient commutation
